sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Namo eWaste is a capital- and working-capital-intensive recycling/refurbishment/EPR business, not a pure asset-light environmental-services platform. Formalization, a larger collection footprint and battery recycling support growth, but cash realization and returns on the IPO-funded expansion are the decisive tests. The company has generated genuine value-add and profits; three-year analytical operating cash is nevertheless negative₹16.16 cr against PAT₹29.64 cr. At₹339.20 the funded moderate-growth model returns 5.43%, well below the 15% hurdle. Classification: Weak setup / value-trap risk, with medium-confidence conditional gates, not an allegation of fraud or a claim that current operations are insolvent. This is an execution-sensitive growth/cyclical research watchlist, not an evidence-backed compounder. Cash-backed commissioning, demonstrable incremental returns and a lower valuation could change the conclusion.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Namo procures discarded electronics, IT equipment and batteries from OEMs, companies, institutions and aggregators, then collects, sorts, dismantles, refurbishes or recycles them. Revenue comes from recovered metal/products, refurbished devices and PRO/EPR or related compliance services; IT asset disposal and data destruction support the proposition. It must finance physical material before selling recovered output or certificates, so metal prices, input competition, recoveries, compliance and collection timing matter as much as headline capacity. FY26 audited revenue: products₹170.6455 cr, PRO/other services₹22.7432 cr and exports₹1.2046 cr. Exports fell from₹11.9798 cr FY25 while domestic product sales rose. Call estimates of₹25 cr EPR, ₹35 cr refurbishment and₹18 crbattery-related sales are rounded management classifications and do not map exactly to audited categories: battery includes₹6 crtrading and₹12 crprocessing, so do not treat all₹18 cr as new manufactured output. Consolidated material cost after inventory change₹150.2336 cr leaves₹44.3597 crgross value-added,22.80% of sales, before staff, transport, utilities and other operating costs. Other income is removed from operating EBIT. Techeco is 99.99%-owned; group financials, not a simple sum of parent and LLP accounts, determine common-owner economics.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Compliance records, certified processing, collection density, OEM relationships and data destruction can lower customer execution risk and freight costs. These are useful capabilities, but no verified exclusive technology, contractual lock-in or sustained superior incremental return establishes a wide moat. The prospectus says no long-term customer contracts; FY24 top 5/top 10 customers were 31.65%/47.49%, down from 48.13%/68.77% FY23, while top 10 suppliers were 78.80% versus 88.46%. Current FY26 concentration is ND, so older diversification cannot be assumed to persist. Formalization is a real demand driver, but it also attracts capacity. Official FY24 recycled volume 768406 tonnes is a flow;386 registered e-waste recyclers and cumulative 28.75 lakh tonnes processed as of March 2026 are different stock/cumulative measures and must not be divided into Namo capacity to invent market share. Neither management's broad TAM nor uncommissioned nameplate capacity is an executable order book. Direct peer Eco Recycling offers ITAD, EPR and recycling; its FY26 audited-style presentation reports₹48.18 crsales, ₹22.88 cr PAT and₹12.90 cr CFO, but its very different service/material mix and other income make margins non-comparable. Gravita is a much larger predominantly metal recycler; its July 2026 presentation distinguishes volume from price and uses hedging-adjusted pre-tax ROIC, unlike this dossier's after-tax measure. Attero's dated 2025 primary supply-chain report documents precious-metal due diligence, supporting a specialist recovery/compliance competitor, not a comparable audited valuation. Peer evidence challenges monopoly-like claims, not a shortcut to copying multiples.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Do not splice FY23 standalone into FY24 consolidated and call the result organic. Techeco joined in April 2023; the post-acquisition consolidated FY24–26 two-year CAGR is 38.85%, but two years is not the preferred 3/5 year scoring window. The defensible longer proxy is parent external revenue:₹58.4460 cr FY23→₹75.0499 cr FY24→₹121.2337 cr FY25→₹135.3087 cr FY26, giving 32.29% three-year CAGR. It removes disclosed parent-to-subsidiary sales but cannot remove all indirect changes from intra-group sourcing; therefore confidence is medium, not high. Parent gross value-added increased from₹9.6386 cr to₹33.0353 cr,50.77% CAGR, corroborating economically meaningful expansion beyond raw sales inflation. FY22 parent external sales₹44.7772 cr provide a four-year historical endpoint, not five-year CAGR. Consolidated annual additions were₹48.9002 cr FY25 and₹44.7613 cr FY26; FY26 group growth 29.87%. Recent parent growth slowed to 13.63%, versus 61.58% FY25. H1FY26 parent sales₹64.2793 cr versus₹52.6125 cr,22.18%; derived H2FY26₹74.3129 cr versus₹69.3588 cr,7.14%. REV starts at 9, receives a minus 1 adjustment for sustained half-year slowing, and is then subject to the shorter-history ceiling 8, leaving final 8. Higher EPR prices, product mix, battery trading and plant ramp are separately disclosed drivers; a precise constant-price/volume organic CAGR is ND, not fabricated. The revenue proxy is accepted only because the material value-add cross-check and realized operating growth are present.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Growth quality is not the same as sales growth. A credible path uses more existing processing capacity and collection reach, rather than capitalizing an unfunded hydromet promise. FY26 headline 82000 MTPA includes Hyderabad 25000 MTPA still described as expected in Q2 FY27 in the annual report; it is not all available FY26 throughput. Management described roughly 36000 MTPA available through FY26,60% utilization; Palwal expansion came only in December. Battery mechanical processing started September 2025 and processed roughly 1200 tonnes, around 10% of nameplate. Existing facilities and a commissioned Hyderabad plant could support higher throughput, but input availability, EPR settlement, technical recovery and customer access are bottlenecks. Base FY27 revenue₹243.24 cr is well below management's approximate₹400 cr ambition, and subsequent growth tapers 25/22/20/18/15%. Terminal TTM₹568.16 cr requires about 2.9 x FY26 sales; this is a modeled scaling case, not contracted demand. No automatic revenue per tonne is imposed across low-value e-waste and high-value battery/ITAD mixes. Full-year EBIT margin moves 11.5%→12%, and operating WC 31.5% of annual revenue plus₹8–12 crannual capex absorbs cash. CAP 5 reflects incremental NOPAT₹7.88 cr on₹58.97 cr additional committed capital,13.37%, close to assumed 12–16% cost, not evidence of a superior reinvestment machine. Cash conversion imposes GQS 5 even though raw growth-quality score is 6.25. Proposed commercial hydromet costs~₹60 cr and management prefers debt; subsidy eligibility is contingent reimbursement, not upfront finance. This is excluded from base and explicitly tested as an unfunded stress.

sections.text: Akshay Jain leads the promoter-controlled business. sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Primary method is a dated operating-earnings terminal-EV model with fully linked working capital, capex, taxes, interest, debt draws/repayments and dilution. It is not an unlevered earnings target that ignores funding. Current market cap₹775.6661 cr, P/E 54.05 x, conservative-cash EV₹778.7723 cr, EV/EBIT 37.80 x and EV/EBITDA 34.51 x; analytical FCFyield is negative and P/B~7.52 x is no liquidation floor. Base 14 x terminal EBIT is deliberately below current multiple and does not borrow Eco Recycling's incomparable margin. Bear/base/bull terminal TTM revenues₹298.17/₹568.16/₹808.90 cr, EBIT margins 8/12/15%, exit multiples 10/14/20, returns-20.22%/5.43%/26.72%. No subjective probabilities or averaged scenario IRR are presented. Terminal equity adds only unrestricted cash above₹2 cr operating reserve, subtracts debt, and adds no property/deposits/subsidy value. Cash ends 20 October 2031, and earnings are trailing 365 days, not full future FY32. ESOP 100000 grants have exerciseprice=marketvalue−₹50: simultaneous terminal pricing transfers₹0.50 cr to options; cash exercise proceeds and 100000 newshares are both modeled, not granted free financing early. Base 15% hurdle price₹219.74;12/18% alternatives₹250.78/₹193.19. These are assumption-dependent prices, not observed fair values. Genuine 3×3×3 WC/capex/multiple sensitivity recalculates all cash rows, with reserve-breached cells returning null. Algebraic reverse expectation requires 32.59% annual growth at 12% margin/14 x and scalingcapex, with residual~0 in 0–80% bracket, but it breaches funding by₹3.76 cr. It is not a financeable hurdle case; the funding-aware solver reports no supported bracket. All ordinary return fields are null after any earlier cash-floor breach. No-new-lines,50%-lines, all FDfree, linkedstress and optional hydromet are separate. A funded hypothetical hydromet rescue issues whole shares upfront at₹100 with 2% fee and explicit dilution/approvals; it is not a forecast. Zero-dividend returns exclude commissions and market impact;1/2/5% roundtrip drag sensitivities are added, while actual spread is ND. Terminal common equity also deducts a conservative 0.01% of total group EV as an upper-bound proxy for the tiny Techeco NCI; this is immaterial but avoids assuming 100% ownership. The optional hydromet rescue exceeds the 25 million authorized shares after 100000 options by the quantified amount in its summary, so it requires authorized-capital increase and shareholder/corporate approvals not assumed already granted.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest positive counterargument is that the IPO build-out temporarily depressed cash while establishing spare capacity, and higher-value battery/EPR work could produce strong incremental margins. Base and ordinary bear are fundable even with much less growth than management's ambition. The strongest negative argument is that greater accounting profits remain tied up in inventory, supplier advances, tax balances and slow receivables, while quoted valuation already assumes rapid economic success. A linked failure is lower EPR realizations or buyer loss→weaker grossspread/utilization→slower collections and more inventory→borrowing/collateral pressure→delayed project or deeply discounted equity. Ordinarybear ends near₹109.67 pershare, roughly 68% belowentry, despite survival; this is valuation/earning-power impairment, not just a temporary drawdown. Linked WC 42%,8% EBITmargin and 50% highercapex breaches funding with a much larger cash requirement. Unfunded hydromet can create a₹44 crorder gap even while the existing business survives. The most important falsifier is sustained cash realization from the current installed base: if two reporting periods show real operating-capital cash improvements with stable margins, the negative cash interpretation weakens; if collection ageing and short-term funding worsen together, a capex story is inadequate. Impairment risk is High at this price, not Certain. Market price-query disclosures do not establish manipulation, and a prudential₹2 crcash floor breach is not an observed insolvency finding.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: No multibagger request is central to this review, so this is a feasibility check, not a speculative price target. Fivefold and tenfold price appreciation over the exact~5 yearhorizon require about 38.0% and 58.5% annual share-price growth. Current P/E 54 x makes extrapolating revenue growth misleading: with a normalized 20 xterminal P/E, stable 7.38% netmargin and 0.44% option-share expansion before proceeds,5×price would need roughly 13.6×revenue and 10×roughly 27.1×, or~69%/~94% annual sales growth from FY26 over a deliberately simplified 5 years. This is a five-year thought experiment, not the dated model: FY26 end to terminal is about 5.55 years. This rough decomposition omits cash/debt changes and is therefore not substituted for the explicit enterprise bridge; it only shows the scale problem. The modeledbull produces~3.27×entryprice, with higher 15% EBITmargin, betterworking capital and 20 x EBIT, already a demanding combination. There is no verified collection/output/funding path supporting 5×or 10×at today'sprice. Outcome classification: Speculative / unsupported on current evidence. Commercial hydromet optionality does not make the capital, technical and counterparty requirements disappear.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor the operating-cash and funding mechanism, not only the share price. The table contains eight company-specific baselines, milestones, alerts and thesis-break conditions. Warning levels are analytical investigation triggers, not universal sell rules or automatic investment decisions. A capacity announcement is not equivalent to commissioning, commissioning is not utilization, and utilization is not cash return on capital. The most informative next evidence is FY27 interim financials with ageing, operating advances and bank-line access, followed by auditedcash conversion. Reassess the implied return with the actual quote and position size before implementation. This is a recommended research cadence only; no reminder, trading instruction or recurring automation has been created.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: The v3 classification is Weak setup / value-trap risk: BQS 5.16 and IAS 3.5900. This describes moderate business quality, poor cash conversion and insufficient modeled return at ₹339.20, not a claim of fraud, worthlessness or certain failure. All four gates are Conditional. No substantiated severe governance failure or present inability to meet mandatory payments was established. Comparison eligibility is not implementation clearance. GQS is capped at 5 and the compounder requirements are not met. Research action: watchlist and wait for better cash evidence, verified facility access and an appropriate price. The base 15% hurdle entry is ₹219.74; a price decline alone would not resolve governance, commissioning or financing gaps. Conversely, operational improvement alone does not guarantee an attractive return from any purchase price. No actual holding, cost basis, portfolio, tax position or risk capacity was supplied, so no allocation or sell instruction is made. If held, distinguish valuation concerns from a demonstrated thesis failure and account for 800 share lots. Display scores are 5.2/5.0/3.6. Small differences among medium-confidence SME scores are not economically decisive.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Audited annual reports, prospectus, official exchange filings, the signed bank agreement, shareholding and official security/bhavcopy records anchor this work. Each source has a date, URL, locator, scope and retrieved-byte hash where available. Company guidance is separated from audited results. Model growth, margins, capital spending, working capital, tax, interest and multiples are analyst assumptions. Original and later financial presentations are retained with reconciliation rather than silently overwritten. The review extends through main audit, CARO, IFC, audit-trail and secretarial annexures, related parties, commitments and accounting notes. Open questions are the amounts behind bank-return differences; Techeco consolidation allocation; current drawing power, renewals and spendable cash; the precise FD restriction split; customer/supplier concentration and connected receivables; project/segment returns; Hyderabad commissioning by cutoff; commercial hydromet economics and committed finance; FY25 weighted EPS denominator; and current bid/ask, ASM/GSM and order-book depth. Later retrieval on 22 October does not move the 20 October information cutoff. Raw source PDFs, OCR, shareholder lists, personal tax identifiers, screenshots, transfer helpers and credentials are excluded from deliverables. Source-safe facts, full model rows and reproducible builders remain available. Precise arithmetic is not a substitute for evidence quality or a prediction guarantee.
